newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end flat after campaign tensions.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end flat after campaign tensions.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended flat on Tuesday as reports of fresh street vilolence between supporters of rival parties campaigning for Indonesia's May 29 general elections erased earlier gains, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 0.28 points, or 0.04 percent, to close at 652.83 points after touching a day's high of 655.81 points. Advancers led decliners by 53 to 49 with 68 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 319 billion rupiah against 293 billion rupiah on Monday.
"The market rebounded in early trading after reports that the PPP had cancelled campaigning, but it failed to sustain the gains after the fresh fighting," one broker said.
Supporters of Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar party clashed in a swathe across southern Jakarta last weekend.
Fresh violence erupted again on Tuesday afternoon despite the PPP's decision to cancel campaigning in the city.
Big-caps Gudang Garam, Tambang Timah and bank BDNI, which had made a modest rebound in noon trading, closed higher, brokers said.
Other big-caps including Sampoerna, Semen Cibinong and Indofood remained among the losers due to weak sentiment, brokers said.
Float glass and ceramics maker Mulia Industrindo ended down 75 rupiah to 1,225 rupiah after it announced lower first quarter net profit, brokers said.
Property firm Mas Murni rose 175 rupiah to close at 825 rupiah on a sudden spurt of active buying near the close due to market talk of a possible take-over, brokers said.
Actively traded footwear manufacturer Kasogi rose 100 rupiah to close at 1,425 rupiah, with 16 million shares traded, on reports of a proposed rights issue, brokers said.
